die() {
    printf '%s: %s\n' "$(basename "$0")" "$*" >&2
    exit 64
}

now_epoch() {
    if [[ -n "${BEACON_NOW:-}" ]]; then
        date -u -d "${BEACON_NOW}" +%s
    else
        date -u +%s
    fi
}

iso_to_epoch() {
    date -u -d "$1" +%s 2>/dev/null || die "bad timestamp: $1"
}

require_status() {

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/common.sh"

usage() {
    cat <<USAGE
Usage: beacon-report [--file FILE] [--date YYYY-MM-DD] [--conditions FILE]

Print the daily report for the lighthouse network: a count of beacons by
state, every beacon that needs a visit, and the fleet's average battery.

Options:
  --file FILE   status file (default: \$BEACON_STATUS_FILE or data/status.txt)
  --date DATE   date printed in the header (default: today, UTC)
  --conditions FILE
                print a Conditions: line per station in FILE, whose lines
                are station|wind|visibility|sea state
  -h, --help    show this help
USAGE
}

file="${BEACON_STATUS_FILE}"
day=""
conditions=""

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --file) file="${2:?--file needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --date) day="${2:?--date needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --conditions) conditions="${2:?--conditions needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) usage >&2; exit 64 ;;
    esac
done

require_status "${file}"
[[ -z "${conditions}" || -r "${conditions}" ]] || die "cannot read ${conditions}"
now="$(now_epoch)"
[[ -n "${day}" ]] || day="$(date -u -d "@${now}" +%F)"

ok=0 warn=0 fail=0 total=0 battery_sum=0
visits=()

while IFS='|' read -r id name lamp last_seen battery; do
    total=$(( total + 1 ))
    battery_sum=$(( battery_sum + battery ))
    seen="$(iso_to_epoch "${last_seen}")"
    age=$(( (now - seen) / 60 ))
    if [[ "${lamp}" != "ok" ]]; then
        fail=$(( fail + 1 ))
        visits+=("${id} ${name}: lamp ${lamp}")
    elif (( age > 30 )); then
        warn=$(( warn + 1 ))
        visits+=("${id} ${name}: silent for ${age} minutes")
    else
        ok=$(( ok + 1 ))
    fi
done < <(read_status "${file}")

(( total > 0 )) || die "no beacons in ${file}"

printf 'Lighthouse network — daily report for %s\n' "${day}"
printf '%s\n' "================================================"
if [[ -n "${conditions}" ]]; then
    while IFS='|' read -r station wind vis sea; do
        [[ -n "${station}" ]] || continue
        printf 'Conditions: %s — wind %s, visibility %s, sea %s\n' "${station}" "${wind}" "${vis}" "${sea}"
    done < "${conditions}"
fi
printf 'beacons: %d   ok: %d   warn: %d   fail: %d\n' "${total}" "${ok}" "${warn}" "${fail}"
printf 'average battery: %d%%\n' $(( battery_sum / total ))
echo
if (( ${#visits[@]} == 0 )); then
    echo "No visits needed."
else
    echo "Needs a visit:"
    printf '  - %s\n' "${visits[@]}"
fi
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
source "$(dirname "$0")/../lib/common.sh"

usage() {
    cat <<USAGE
Usage: beacon-status [--file FILE] [--stale-minutes N] [--quiet]

Check every beacon in the status file and print one line each:

  OK     lamp lit, heard from recently, battery healthy
  WARN   stale (no report for N minutes) or battery below 20%
  FAIL   lamp reported anything other than "ok"

Options:
  --file FILE         status file (default: \$BEACON_STATUS_FILE or data/status.txt)
  --stale-minutes N   minutes of silence before a beacon is stale (default: 30)
  --quiet             print only beacons that are not OK
  -h, --help          show this help

Exit status: 0 all OK, 1 any WARN, 2 any FAIL, 64 usage error.
USAGE
}

file="${BEACON_STATUS_FILE}"
stale_minutes=30
quiet=false

while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
    case "$1" in
        --file) file="${2:?--file needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --stale-minutes) stale_minutes="${2:?--stale-minutes needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
        --quiet) quiet=true; shift ;;
        -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
        *) usage >&2; exit 64 ;;
    esac
done

[[ "${stale_minutes}" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] || die "--stale-minutes must be a whole number"

require_status "${file}"
now="$(now_epoch)"
worst=0

while IFS='|' read -r id name lamp last_seen battery; do
    state=OK
    notes=()
    if [[ "${lamp}" != "ok" ]]; then
        state=FAIL
        notes+=("lamp ${lamp}")
    fi
    seen="$(iso_to_epoch "${last_seen}")"
    age=$(( (now - seen) / 60 ))
    if (( age > stale_minutes )); then
        [[ "${state}" == FAIL ]] || state=WARN
        notes+=("silent ${age}m")
    fi
    if (( 10#${battery} < 20 )); then
        [[ "${state}" == FAIL ]] || state=WARN
        notes+=("battery ${battery}%")
    fi

    case "${state}" in
        WARN) (( worst < 1 )) && worst=1 ;;
        FAIL) worst=2 ;;
    esac

    if [[ "${quiet}" == true && "${state}" == OK ]]; then
        continue
    fi
    printf '%-4s  %-6s %-18s %s\n' "${state}" "${id}" "${name}" "${notes[*]:-}"
done < <(read_status "${file}")

exit "${worst}"
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
    cat <<USAGE
Usage: test/run.sh [--help] [PATTERN]

Run every test_* function in this file whose name matches PATTERN
(default: all). Each test runs in its own subshell and scratch directory.
USAGE
}

[[ "${1:-}" == "-h" || "${1:-}" == "--help" ]] && { usage; exit 0; }
pattern="${1:-}"

HERE="$(cd -- "$(dirname "$0")" >/dev/null && pwd)"
BIN="${HERE}/../bin"
FIXTURES="${HERE}/fixtures"
export BEACON_NOW="2026-10-07T06:00:00Z"

fail() { echo "    $*" >&2; return 1; }

assert_eq() {
    [[ "$1" == "$2" ]] || fail "expected [$2], got [$1]"
}

assert_contains() {
    [[ "$1" == *"$2"* ]] || fail "expected output to contain [$2], got:"$'\n'"$1"
}

assert_file() {
    [[ -e "$1" ]] || fail "expected $1 to exist"
}

assert_no_file() {
    [[ ! -e "$1" ]] || fail "expected $1 not to exist"
}

status_exit() {
    local code=0
    "${BIN}/beacon-status" "$@" >/dev/null 2>&1 || code=$?
    echo "${code}"
}

test_status_when_every_beacon_is_healthy_it_should_exit_0() {
    assert_eq "$(status_exit --file "${FIXTURES}/all-ok.txt")" 0
}

test_status_when_a_lamp_is_not_ok_it_should_exit_2() {
    assert_eq "$(status_exit --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt")" 2
}

test_status_when_a_lamp_is_dim_it_should_mark_it_failed() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" || true)" "FAIL  BX03"
}

test_status_when_a_beacon_is_silent_it_should_warn_with_the_age() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" || true)" "silent 120m"
}

test_status_when_the_battery_is_low_it_should_warn() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" || true)" "battery 12%"
}

test_status_when_the_stale_window_is_widened_it_should_not_warn() {
    local out
    out="$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" --stale-minutes 180 || true)"
    [[ "${out}" != *"silent"* ]] || fail "still reported silent beacons"
}

test_status_when_the_battery_is_100_percent_it_should_not_warn() {
    local out
    out="$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/battery.txt" || true)"
    [[ "${out}" != *"battery 100%"* ]] || fail "warned about a full battery:"$'\n'"${out}"
}

test_status_when_the_battery_is_single_digit_it_should_warn() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/battery.txt" || true)" "battery 9%"
}

test_status_when_quiet_it_should_omit_ok_beacons() {
    local out
    out="$("${BIN}/beacon-status" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" --quiet || true)"
    [[ "${out}" != *"BX01"* ]] || fail "printed an OK beacon"
}

test_status_when_the_file_is_missing_it_should_exit_64() {
    assert_eq "$(status_exit --file "${SCRATCH}/nope.txt")" 64
}

test_report_when_run_it_should_count_beacons_by_state() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-report" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt")" "beacons: 5   ok: 3   warn: 1   fail: 1"
}

test_report_when_run_it_should_average_the_battery() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-report" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt")" "average battery: 52%"
}

test_report_when_a_date_is_given_it_should_put_it_in_the_header() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-report" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" --date 2026-01-31)" "report for 2026-01-31"
}

test_report_when_nothing_needs_a_visit_it_should_say_so() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-report" --file "${FIXTURES}/all-ok.txt")" "No visits needed."
}

test_report_when_conditions_are_given_it_should_print_a_line_per_station() {
    local out
    out="$("${BIN}/beacon-report" --file "${FIXTURES}/status.txt" --conditions "${FIXTURES}/conditions.txt")"
    assert_contains "${out}" "Conditions: Carrick Point — wind S 21 kn, visibility 10 nm, sea rough" || return 1
    assert_contains "${out}" "Conditions: Porthwenna Head — wind NE 9 kn, visibility 9 nm, sea moderate"
}

make_logs() {
    mkdir -p "${SCRATCH}/logs"
    echo "today" > "${SCRATCH}/logs/carrick.log"
    echo "yesterday" > "${SCRATCH}/logs/carrick.log.1"
    echo "oldest" > "${SCRATCH}/logs/carrick.log.2"
}

test_rotate_when_run_it_should_shift_the_current_log_to_1() {
    make_logs
    "${BIN}/beacon-rotate" --dir "${SCRATCH}/logs" --keep 3 >/dev/null
    assert_eq "$(cat "${SCRATCH}/logs/carrick.log.1")" "today"
}

test_rotate_when_run_it_should_leave_an_empty_current_log() {
    make_logs
    "${BIN}/beacon-rotate" --dir "${SCRATCH}/logs" --keep 3 >/dev/null
    [[ ! -s "${SCRATCH}/logs/carrick.log" ]] || fail "current log is not empty"
}

test_rotate_when_past_keep_it_should_drop_the_oldest() {
    make_logs
    "${BIN}/beacon-rotate" --dir "${SCRATCH}/logs" --keep 2 >/dev/null
    assert_eq "$(cat "${SCRATCH}/logs/carrick.log.2")" "yesterday"
}

test_rotate_when_dry_run_it_should_change_nothing() {
    make_logs
    "${BIN}/beacon-rotate" --dir "${SCRATCH}/logs" --dry-run >/dev/null
    assert_eq "$(cat "${SCRATCH}/logs/carrick.log")" "today"
}

test_rotate_when_keep_is_zero_it_should_refuse() {
    make_logs
    local code=0
    "${BIN}/beacon-rotate" --dir "${SCRATCH}/logs" --keep 0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || code=$?
    assert_eq "${code}" 64
}

test_rotate_when_there_are_no_logs_it_should_say_so() {
    assert_contains "$("${BIN}/beacon-rotate" --dir "${SCRATCH}")" "nothing to rotate"
}

test_every_script_when_asked_for_help_it_should_print_usage() {
    local script
    for script in "${BIN}"/*; do
        assert_contains "$("${script}" --help)" "Usage: $(basename "${script}")" || return 1
    done
}

passed=0 failed=0
for t in $(declare -F | awk '{print $3}' | grep '^test_'); do
    [[ -z "${pattern}" || "${t}" == *${pattern}* ]] || continue
    SCRATCH="$(mktemp -d)"
    if ( set -e; SCRATCH="${SCRATCH}"; "${t}" ); then
        passed=$(( passed + 1 ))
        echo "ok   ${t}"
    else
        failed=$(( failed + 1 ))
        echo "FAIL ${t}"
    fi
    rm -rf "${SCRATCH}"
done

echo
echo "${passed} passed, ${failed} failed"
(( failed == 0 ))

Both scripts now share one classifier, `classify_beacon` in `lib/common.sh`, and `bash test/run.sh` passes (22 of 22).

- **Classifier:** it takes the lamp state, age in minutes, battery and an optional stale window (default 30). It sets `BEACON_STATE` (OK, WARN or FAIL) and `BEACON_NOTES`. The rules are the ones `beacon-status` already used.
- **`beacon-status`:** it calls the shared function and still honours `--stale-minutes`.
- **`beacon-report`:** it calls the same function, so it now has the battery check and the stale window instead of its own hard-coded 30. The "Needs a visit" lines now list the shared notes, so the wording changed from "silent for 120 minutes" to "silent 120m" and "battery 12%".
- **Battery arithmetic:** the report's battery sum now uses `10#`, as `beacon-status` already did. Without it, a zero-padded value like `08` would break the arithmetic.

**Changed test:** the report's state-count test changed from `ok: 3 warn: 1 fail: 1` to `ok: 2 warn: 2 fail: 1`. The old numbers counted BX05 (12% battery) as OK, which is the drift this ticket is about. The change is in `test/run.sh`, which already had uncommitted edits from you.

content.content:
# beacon

Shell tooling for the coastal lighthouse network.
Each beacon reports its lamp state, the last time it was heard from and its battery level, and these scripts turn that into something a keeper can act on.

## Scripts

| script | does |
| --- | --- |
| `bin/beacon-status` | one line per beacon: `OK`, `WARN` or `FAIL`, and why |
| `bin/beacon-report` | the daily report: counts by state, who needs a visit, average battery |
| `bin/beacon-rotate` | rotates the lamp logs in `data/logs/` and keeps the last seven |

Every script takes `--help`.

## Quick start

```sh
make status
make report
make rotate     # a dry run; call bin/beacon-rotate directly to rotate for real
make test
```

`BEACON_STATUS_FILE` and `BEACON_LOG_DIR` point the scripts at other data.
`BEACON_NOW` pins the clock, which is how the tests stay deterministic.

## Exit codes

`beacon-status` exits 0 when every beacon is `OK`, 1 when any is `WARN`, and 2 when any is `FAIL`.
All scripts exit 64 on a usage error.

## Tests

`test/run.sh` is plain bash with no framework.
It runs every `test_*` function in its own subshell and scratch directory, and takes an optional pattern to run a subset.
